audit_findings.title: Post-Eddyfi numerator and capital structure describe different claims
audit_findings.magnitude: Net unquantified; post-close debt is $2,416.614 million, $1,173.399 million above year-end 2025, and annual MCPS dividends compute to $11.375 million; Eddyfi consideration was $1,494.014 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE numerator excludes Eddyfi earnings, post-close interest and MCPS dividends, while the share count, cash and capital structure reflect the completed acquisition.
audit_findings.evidence: The acquisition is expected to be funded with a combination of cash on hand, debt and approximately $318 million of fully committed equity.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible error. Excluding Eddyfi earnings understates value, while excluding the associated interest and preferred dividends overstates it. The net direction cannot be determined, but the acquisition and financing are large relative to the $211.4 million anchor and are reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rerun on one coherent post-close basis using seasoned Eddyfi OE, recurring interest on each post-close borrowing, the $11.375 million annual MCPS dividend until conversion, and the applicable common-share conversion range; reconcile the result to the filed pro-forma financials and prevent double counting of equity proceeds or preferred conversion shares.

audit_findings.title: Legacy asbestos costs may be missing from both the forecast and bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Known July 2026 net recorded claim is $54.616 million, comprising $298.926 million of liabilities less $244.310 million of insurance assets; cash outflows were $15.0 million in 2025 and $11.8 million in the first half of 2026; post-15-year tail unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Value is overstated if asbestos losses and cash outflows were excluded from OE while the net recorded liability and unaccrued tail were also omitted from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, no accrual has been recorded for any costs that may be paid after the next 15 years.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, but the OE treatment is not supplied. The recorded net claim alone equals about $0.82 per diluted share and 1.7% of base equity value. However, 2025 cash outflow equals 7.1% of the OE anchor, the first-half 2026 outflow was already $11.8 million, and the post-15-year tail cannot be estimated from the record. Materiality therefore remains unresolved rather than disproved.
audit_findings.action: Trace settlement, defense, insurance-recovery and discontinued-operation cash flows through each OE reconciliation. Then either retain a normalized net annual cash cost in OE or deduct the latest net asbestos obligation plus a supportable tail estimate from the bridge, without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may include trapped or non-distributable cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $50 million of Russian cash, or about $0.75 per diluted share; the entire $217.491 million cash balance is about $3.27 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted, operational or minority-claimed cash would reduce the cash added to operating value in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Excluding any goodwill allocation, Russia has approximately 5% of our total net assets as of December 31, 2025, including approximately $50 million of Cash and cash equivalents that may be subject to delays in withdrawing from Russia, based upon the current environment at that time.
audit_findings.explanation: The Russian amount is subject to withdrawal delays, and $194.9 million of total cash was held outside the United States. Nevertheless, even removing the entire $217.491 million add-back would reduce value by only about $3.27 per share, lowering bull value from $53.15 to about $49.88 versus the $75.02 market price. The known and maximum cash-add-back exposure therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: For precision, classify cash by jurisdiction, legal availability, operating need, tax leakage and minority claims, then replace the bridge add-back with distributable excess cash; no conclusion-changing rerun is required.

audit_findings.title: Recurring restructuring and serial-acquisition costs cannot be normalized away
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 restructuring and transaction, diligence and integration charges totaled $59.256 million, equal to 28.0% of the $211.4 million anchor; corresponding first-half 2026 charges totaled $63.578 million; sustainable normalized amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding recurring restructuring and acquisition-related cash spending back to OE raises the anchor and capitalizes those exclusions through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We have implemented, and plan to continue to implement, restructuring programs designed to facilitate key strategic initiatives and maintain long-term sustainable growth.
audit_findings.explanation: The OE reconciliation is not supplied, so an improper add-back is not yet demonstrated. Recurrence is demonstrated: restructuring and acquisition-related charges occurred throughout the historical period and accelerated in 2025 and 2026. Given their scale relative to the anchor and ESAB's stated acquisition-led strategy, an omitted normalized allowance is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every annual OE adjustment for restructuring, transaction, diligence and integration costs. Establish a normalized recurring cash allowance from the filed multi-year history, remove only specifically supported nonrecurring items, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: The pension deficit is a senior cash claim absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $34.290 million net underfunding and $5.2 million expected 2026 contributions; the full deficit equals about $0.52 per diluted share and 1.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any contribution requirement exceeding pension expense retained in OE reduces forecast OE; alternatively, an uncovered deficit reduces common equity through the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Expected contributions to the Company’s pension benefit plans for the year ending December 31, 2026 are $5.2 million.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether forecast OE already captures the relevant cash burden is unresolved, but the maximum directly filed bridge adjustment is modest. Deducting the full $34.290 million deficit would lower base value from $47.94 to about $47.42 per share and would not alter the conclusion relative to the $75.02 market price. Expected 2026 contributions are only 2.5% of the OE anchor.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether OE captures employer contributions rather than only accounting pension expense. If not, model the contribution schedule or deduct the after-tax uncovered deficit, while avoiding duplication between OE and the bridge.

audit_findings.title: A disposal gain may have been capitalized in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.645 million pretax and approximately $4.454 million after tax using the filed 21.1% effective tax rate, equal to 2.1% of the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in anchor OE, the nonrecurring property-sale gain is projected and capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Selling, general and administrative expense increased over the same period primarily due to acquisitions and related costs partially offset by a gain on disposition of property.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied record does not demonstrate whether the gain remains in OE. Even assuming the full after-tax amount is embedded, removing it would reduce computed scenario values by approximately $0.80 per share in bear, $0.94 in base and $1.05 in bull. Bull value would remain about $52.10 versus the $75.02 market price, so this item cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $211.4 million anchor to the cash-flow statement and the $5.645 million gain. Remove the approximately $4.454 million after-tax effect if embedded, then update scenario values and the margin-of-safety threshold.
